source.title: Genomic Next-Token Predictors are In-Context Learners
source.authors: Nathan Breslow; Aayush Mishra; M. Schatz; An-Qi Liu; Mahler Revsine; Daniel Khashabi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares task accuracy across model sizes, bearing on V6, but does not measure held-out cross-entropy or test the original loss-scaling method.
record.gate_note: The study reports accuracy on prompted symbolic reasoning tasks across model sizes and shot counts. It does not report held-out pretraining cross-entropy, fitted loss exponents, predictions from small runs, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations; the cited Kaplan compute estimate is background for compute matching, not a test of those findings.
record.test_reason: The scale result is secondary but real. The paper regresses accuracy on a new synthetic in-context task on parameter count across off-the-shelf model families (Qwen3 0.6B–14B; Evo2 1B–40B). It reports a significant positive slope for Qwen3 at ≥16 shots and a plateau for Evo2 beyond 7B. That bears on V6 in a new setting: symbolic ICL tasks and a genomic model family. It is not T2, because there is no loss measurement and no scaling-law fit. The Kaplan 6ND estimate is used only for compute matching.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but misses the main point. The authors' central conclusion is that a genomic model (Evo2) shows organically emergent in-context learning, with log-linear gains in demonstrations paralleling Qwen3. They take this as evidence that ICL is modality-agnostic, not language-specific. On scale, they report that Qwen3 accuracy correlates positively with parameter count, while Evo2 jumps from 1B to 7B with little gain beyond. They suggest saturation once capacity suffices. They draw no conclusions about loss scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.recipe_differences: Measures exact-match accuracy on few-shot symbolic tasks across pretrained model sizes, rather than held-out cross-entropy across controlled parameter, token, and compute sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy varies with model family and size; the paper reports non-monotonic shot-count patches for Qwen3 and a plateau between Evo2 7B and 40B.

fits_no_version.finding: Accuracy rises log-linearly with the number of in-context demonstrations for all models (slopes significant, p≤1e-3). On the promoter task, a saturated power law in shots fits Evo2 7B with R²=0.998.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context accuracy scales log-linearly or as a saturating power law in the number of demonstrations, across text and genomic models.

fits_no_version.finding: The log-shot regression slope (ICL efficacy) rises with parameter count: it more than doubles from Qwen3 0.6B to 14B and rises mildly for Evo2. The intercept is roughly constant at about 0.12.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With model scale, the rate of in-context improvement per demonstration increases, rather than zero-shot accuracy.

record.problems: The results concern a specific symbolic in-context task suite rather than downstream benchmarks or pretraining loss. The authors note that the cross-family prompting setup may favor Evo2; task-level estimates use only m=8 Monte Carlo trials, which they say reduces the significance of task-level comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining shot-count accuracy entries in Appendix C, Table 4, and the promoter-classification shot sweep in Appendix E are not included because they do not add a parameter-scaling result for V6. The mode-baseline and shuffled-label comparisons are also omitted because they test the presence of in-context learning rather than performance scaling with model size.

untested.parts: Held-out loss vs parameters, tokens or compute; no loss is measured.
No fits or extrapolation from small runs.
No fixed-parameter shape comparisons. The Hyena versus transformer contrast is across families and is confounded.
No loss power law for genomic models. The study reports only task accuracy.
No prediction from pretraining loss and no fitted functional form in scale. Standard downstream benchmarks are not used. There are only 3–5 sizes per family.

missing.what: Low-shot accuracies by model size, showing no scale trend at 1–4 shots and non-monotonic order at 8 shots. rows_left_out wrongly says these add no parameter-scaling result.
Significance of the accuracy-vs-parameter slope: Qwen3 p<0.05 for shots ≥16; Evo2 jump then little improvement.
Log-shot slope (ICL efficacy) versus parameters for each family.

record.verdict_notes: The scale comparison uses off-the-shelf models. For Evo2, tokens co-vary with size (1T, 2.4T, 9.3T); Qwen3 holds tokens at 36T. Only 3–5 sizes per family, overlapping standard errors (about ±3 points), and m=8 Monte Carlo trials limit any claim of predictability. Evo2 is a genomic model, so its rows bear on V6 outside text. The authors concede the prompt setup may favour Evo2. The tranche is changed from T2 to T3.

Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their trends with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count and their effect on loss.

The study tests accuracy on its own symbolic in-context tasks across parameter sizes, not broad downstream benchmarks or performance predicted from pretraining loss.

rows.subject: Qwen3-0.6B-Base
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated exact-match accuracy on few-shot bitstring program-synthesis tasks.
rows.note: Part of the reported Qwen3 accuracy trend across parameter sizes at 128 shots.
rows.check: This is the smallest-model reference point of the Qwen3 trend, not an effect on its own. Its state is set by comparison with r2–r5. The baseline should read 'reference: smallest Qwen3'.

rows.check: Baseline should be r1. The total gain from 0.6B to 14B is about 10 points (23.6 to 33.8).

rows.subject: Evo2 1B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated exact-match accuracy on few-shot bitstring program-synthesis tasks.
rows.note: Evo2 accuracy rises from 1B to 7B at 128 shots.
rows.check: This is the reference point for the Evo2 trend. Evo2 is a genomic model, so it bears on V6 only in a non-text setting.

rows.subject: Evo2 7B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated exact-match accuracy on few-shot bitstring program-synthesis tasks.
rows.note: Evo2 accuracy rises from 1B to 7B at 128 shots.
rows.check: Baseline should be r6 (Evo2 1B, 30.8%). Training tokens also change with size (1T to 2.4T), so the gain is not parameter-only.

rows.subject: Evo2 40B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated exact-match accuracy on few-shot bitstring program-synthesis tasks.
rows.note: Accuracy is nearly unchanged from Evo2 7B, consistent with the authors' reported plateau beyond 7B.
rows.check: Relative to r7 (41.0%), 41.1% is no change. Tokens rise from 2.4T to 9.3T and parameters about 6x, yet accuracy is flat. The authors call the curves 'near-indistinguishable'. This is absent, not partial.

relationships.condition: Qwen3 base models (0.6B–14B, all trained on 36T tokens), 128 shots and generally ≥16 shots
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises monotonically with parameter count, from 23.6% to 33.8% (r1–r5). The text reports p<0.05 for the slope at all shot counts ≥16.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased at each tested size from 23.6% to 33.8% at 128 shots, with positive size slopes reported at p<0.05 for every shot setting ≥16.

relationships.reason: Accuracy jumps from 1B to 7B (r6→r7) but is flat from 7B to 40B (41.0% vs 41.1%, r8), despite more parameters and tokens. Improvement with scale saturates.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy changed only from 41.0% to 41.1% between Evo2 7B and 40B despite additional parameters and training tokens.

relationships.condition: Low shot counts (1–8 shots), both families
relationships.reason: Based on the text (Table 4), not on rows. At 1 shot Qwen3 spans only 13.4–14.0% across 0.6B–14B. At 8 shots the order is non-monotonic (4B 15.4% vs 0.6B 19.5%). Scale gains appear only with many demonstrations.
relationships.display_finding: At one demonstration, Qwen3 accuracy spanned only 13.4–14.0% across 0.6B–14B models; at eight, 4B scored 15.4% versus 19.5% for 0.6B.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy increases across the tested Qwen3 parameter sizes, from 23.6±2.9% to 33.8±3.5% (r1–r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy increases from 1B to 7B but is essentially flat from 7B to 40B (r6–r8).
